previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a left knee debridement and cement spacer replacement complicated by unexpected 1200 mL blood loss, leading to acute blood loss anemia. She was initially intubated and transfused multiple units of packed red blood cells due to a difficult crossmatch. Cultures confirmed MSSA and Group B Streptococcus joint infection, prompting a switch to IV cefazolin. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. She developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea, managed with loperamide and diphenoxylate-atropine, and a concurrent E. coli UTI treated by cefazolin. Warfarin was initiated for DVT prophylaxis with close INR monitoring due to tacrolimus interaction. Her kidney function and acidosis improved, and she was discharged home with home health services for six weeks of IV antibiotics, follow-up labs, and wound care instructions.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  PICC placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, the right IJ catheter has been
removed and replaced with a PICC line that extends to the upper portion of the
SVC.  Continued prominence of the cardiac silhouette without definite
atelectatic change or consolidation.

INDICATION:  History of bilateral lower extremity edema.  Please evaluate for
DVT.

COMPARISONS:  DVT study from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, color, spectral Doppler evaluation of the bilateral
lower extremity veins was performed.

FINDINGS:  

There is symmetric respiratory variation in the right and left common femoral
veins.  Appropriate flow and compression is demonstrated in the right common
femoral, proximal superficial femoral, mid superficial femoral, distal
superficial femoral, and popliteal veins.  The right calf veins could not be
visualized.

Appropriate compression was demonstrated in the left common femoral, proximal
superficial femoral, and mid superficial femoral veins.  The patient could not
tolerate compression of the left distal superficial femoral vein; however,
appropriate wall-to-wall flow was demonstrated in this vein.  The patient
would not allow for examination of her left popliteal vein.  The left
posterior tibial and peroneal veins demonstrated normal wall-to-wall color
flow.

There is marked edema in the bilateral lower extremities.

IMPRESSION:  

No evidence of a DVT in the visualized veins bilaterally.  

NOTE: In the right lower extremity, the calf veins could not be visualized. 
In the left lower extremity, the patient would not allow examination of her
popliteal vein.

HISTORY:  Right upper extremity PICC line, redness, pain, induration. 
Evaluate for infection or thrombophlebitis.

COMPARISON:  None available.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images were
obtained of the right upper extremity veins.

FINDINGS:  The right internal jugular and axillary veins are patent and
compressible with transducer pressure.  There is normal flow with respiratory
variation in the bilateral subclavian veins.  The right brachial and cephalic
veins are patent and compressible with transducer pressure and demonstrate
normal color flow and augmentation.  There is a small amount of non-occlusive
clot surrounding a focal portion of a central venous catheter within the right
basilic vein in the upper arm.

IMPRESSION:  Small amount of non-occlusive echogenic clot surrounding a
central venous catheter in the right basilic vein in the upper arm.

Results were discussed over the telephone with Dr. ___ by Dr.
___ at 5:47 p.m. ___, two minutes after discovery.

RADIOGRAPHS OF THE LEFT KNEE

HISTORY:  Left knee infection and dehiscence status post irrigation and
debridement with placement of antibiotic spacer.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Left knee, AP and cross-table lateral portable views.

FINDINGS:  Soft tissue swelling is markedly reduced.  There is again an
antibiotic spacer interposed between the femur and tibia.  Intramedullary
wires have been placed since the prior study in the distal femur since the
prior study, and a wire with antibiotic beads in the proximal tibia has been
replaced.  New drains terminate in the suprapatellar region and along the
proximal anterior tibia.The extent of lucency in the distal femoral stump
appears unchanged.  There is somewhat better defined periosteal reaction along
the distal anterior shaft of the femur while periosteal reaction about the
patella appears similar.

IMPRESSION:  Status post revision with impregnated antibiotic beads in the
femoral and tibial shafts as well as a large spacer between the bones.  No
increase in the extent of bone destruction.
